tldr: Anthropic and cloud partners started shipping a self-hosted "Claude apps gateway" this month, beginning with Google Cloud on Jul 1. It gives organizations a single control plane for access, cost, and policy over Claude Code and Claude Desktop, replacing ad hoc per-developer setup.
whats_new: AWS shipped its own Claude apps gateway on Jul 8, and InfoQ's Jul 15 coverage names the specific capabilities: centralized identity, policy, telemetry, routing, and spend caps for Claude Code and Claude Desktop.
why_it_matters: Any team running Claude Code or Desktop org-wide on AWS or GCP now has a supported, self-hosted admin layer instead of building their own proxy for spend caps, routing, and access policy.

status.detail: Available self-hosted on both Google Cloud (Jul 1) and AWS (Jul 8); latest coverage frames it as the control-plane layer for governing Claude Code and Claude Desktop deployments.

beats.headline: Google Cloud ships the first Claude apps gateway
beats.summary: A self-hosted control plane replacing the ad hoc per-developer CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX setup with centralized access, cost, and policy management.

beats.headline: AWS ships its own Claude apps gateway
beats.summary: Same self-hosted control-plane pattern extended to AWS, giving organizations a single point of control over access, cost, and policy for Claude Code and Claude Desktop.

beats.headline: Coverage details the AWS gateway's control-plane capabilities
beats.summary: InfoQ's writeup names identity, policy, telemetry, routing, and spend caps as the specific functions the self-hosted gateway centralizes.

open_questions: Does the Claude apps gateway extend to Azure or other clouds?
What granularity of spend-cap and policy control does it actually support in production?
Any published enterprise adoption or usage data since launch?
take_for_builders: If you're deploying Claude Code or Desktop org-wide on AWS or GCP, evaluate the vendor-shipped gateway before building your own proxy for identity, routing, and spend caps.
